- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overshoot — cap upward revisions within 3–5 days to prevent overcorrection.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model underreacts — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% of recent range.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model often underestimates downside risk — add 1–3% buffer below forecast.  
- If recent auction events are frequent (≥3/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate bullish momentum — reduce forecast by 1–3% per event.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above 30d mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is bearish and supply net is negative, model often fails to capture full downside — add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.  
- When sentiment is bullish but supply net is negative, model often overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with supply constraints.
